judged_text: In sync mode the body returned by handleWebexResponse is the sync endpoint's `{access_token, expiry_date}` payload, which lacks the webex token-response fields (refresh_token, expires_in) the adapter reads to rebuild the credential key. Webex credentials are re-stored without valid expiry/refresh data, so webex meeting creation degrades to failures once the initial access token expires.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts`, `refreshAccessToken` was switched to use `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and then passes the returned `response` into `handleWebexResponse(response, credential.id)`. In sync mode, `refreshOAuthTokens` bypasses the provider refresh call and instead POSTs to `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, with an in-code comment stating the endpoint “should only contain the access token and expiry date”. Unlike other adapters updated in this diff (e.g., Zoom/Office365/Google) Webex was not updated to use `parseRefreshTokenResponse` or any logic to accept/normalize this minimal `{access_token, expiry_date}` shape. Therefore, in sync mode the Webex adapter is very likely to receive a non-Webex token response shape (missing fields like `expires_in` and potentially `refresh_token`) and proceed as if it were a Webex token response, which would lead to storing/using incomplete credential data and break once the access token expires.
